title: Answer to Question: The Removal of Musharraf from Power
text:
Answer to Question: The Removal of Musharraf from Power

Question: It was previously repeated by American officials that Musharraf is a “treasure” for the United States of America in preserving their interests and strengthening their influence in the region, and that he was a decisive factor for them in the occupation of Afghanistan... And yesterday, 18/8/2008 CE, America lets him be removed from power (resign). So how is that? Or is there a political struggle with Britain, which resulted in Britain's success in removing Musharraf? Then who is expected to replace Musharraf in the presidency of the republic?

Answer: Yes, Musharraf was a “treasure” for the United States, a treasure indeed. He provided services to America in Afghanistan and the region; we may not be exaggerating if we say that America would not have occupied Afghanistan were it not for the help of Musharraf. This is in addition to his confronting the Muslims resisting the occupation, under the pretext of “combating terrorism”, which made it easy for America to arrest a number of the Muslims resisting the occupation...

All of this is true, but Musharraf in recent years, and especially for a year or so, was no longer able to implement America's plans. He became incapable of that because of the shaking of his position, whether among the people, in the army or in parliament. That was because of the multitude of his crimes against the Muslims, especially his massacres in the tribal area and the Swat Valley, and his massacres in the Red Mosque, and his exposed eagerness to throw himself into America's embrace and to offer it every service he could, defying not only the thoughts and concepts of the Muslims but even their feelings...

The statements of some American officials revealed Musharraf's inability to carry out his tasks in the way America wants, as a result of the shaking of his position in the government, the army and the Ummah. Among these statements is what the commander of the American forces in Afghanistan, General David McKiernan, said on 7/8/2008 CE to the American television station (CNN): “Do I believe there is some form of collusion on the part of the Pakistani intelligence service? Yes, I believe so.” McKiernan added: “We have seen an increasing number of foreign fighters in southern and eastern Afghanistan this year, and we are waiting for the authorities in Pakistan to move against their safe havens.”

The newspaper (The New York Times) had mentioned that Steve Kappes, the second man in the American Central Intelligence Agency (CIA), went to Islamabad to request clarifications from the Pakistani authorities and to present them with evidence of the collusion of Pakistani intelligence with the insurgency network led by Jalaluddin Haqqani.

The newspaper affirmed: “The Americans monitored communications that apparently prove the involvement of some elements of Pakistani intelligence in the attack on the Indian embassy in Kabul, which resulted in the killing of sixty people.”

Thus it became clear to America that the shaking of Musharraf's position in his relationship with the army, the government and the people does not enable him to perform his duty as America wants, despite the sacrifice and devotion Musharraf expends in serving America.

Accordingly, America saw that Musharraf had exhausted his role, and that there must be an alternative who appears to the people as their rescuer from Musharraf's dictatorship, and who then achieves America's interests, preserves their influence and continues fighting the Muslims under the pretext of combating terrorism... that is, who repeats Musharraf's course in serving America when he was holding power strongly, before his star fell and he resigned!

It is worth mentioning that the removal (resignation) of Musharraf yesterday was not the product of its day. Rather, Musharraf's star began to fall gradually through four stations; his star dimmed little by little at each station until it was extinguished by the announcement of his resignation on 18/8/2008 CE.

These stations are:

The first station: it was when America made a deal with Britain under which it allowed Benazir Bhutto, the leader of the People's Party, to return from her exile in Britain to Pakistan. The most prominent things in the deal were two matters:

First: that the People's Party would not object to the re-election of Musharraf as President of the Republic.

Second: the sharing of power with Musharraf, by her being Prime Minister with effective powers.

That is, America realised that Musharraf could not continue in power except with the support of Benazir's secular party for him, because of Musharraf's massacres against the Muslims and their hatred of him. Thus America saw in this deal the rescue of what could be rescued of Musharraf's authority, even if it were diminished.

It is worth mentioning that the People's Party is an “aggregating” party and not a bloc party; that is, it has no defined thoughts in which its members believe and around which they form a bloc. Rather, it is an aggregation of persons according to certain interests and relevant circumstances, and for this reason it is easy to penetrate, and this is what has appeared in it. In the era of Bhutto the father, America was behind the People's Party, but Britain was able, during the years of Benazir Bhutto's exile there, to win her loyalty and the loyalty of influential leaders in the People's Party, and Britain came to influence it on its side, after it had been loyal to America in the era of Bhutto the father.

Accordingly, the first station was this deal that returned Benazir Bhutto to Pakistan, with the diminishing of Musharraf's authority.

As for the second station: it was the day America allowed Nawaz Sharif to return to Pakistan. Nawaz Sharif is one of America's men, but it became angry with him when he did not prevent the Pakistani army from occupying the Kargil heights in India during the rule of the Janata Party led by Vajpayee, the former Prime Minister of India.

It is well known that America exerted every effort until it won the loyalty of the Janata Party after the long years of the Congress Party's rule of India, which is a party loyal to the English.

America was supporting Vajpayee economically, politically and militarily to prolong his era, so the occupation of the Kargil heights came as the driving of a wedge into the popularity of the Janata Party.

Therefore America was behind Musharraf's coup against Nawaz Sharif and his expulsion, and America remained angry with him and would not allow him to return.

However, the rise of the People's Party's stock to the heights of the sky, “especially after the assassination of Bhutto”, this rise created a fear in America that the People's Party would sweep the voters' votes, and then not abide by the terms of the deal, seize power alone, and Britain's influence would return...

Therefore it allowed Nawaz to return to Pakistan so that his party would share the people's resentment of Musharraf, share it with the People's Party, so that the votes would not all go to the People's Party, but the majority would be distributed between Bhutto's party and Nawaz Sharif's party.

This is the second station, and it was clear from the return of Nawaz Sharif that matters had begun to be prepared for what comes after Musharraf.

As for the third station: it was America's instruction to Musharraf to give up command of the army to facilitate his election, the army that he used to exploit as a source of strength in every popular or parliamentary crisis facing him.

As for the fourth, decisive station: it is the visit of Pakistan's current Prime Minister Raza Gilani to America, his lengthy meeting with Bush, then his return to Pakistan and his commencement of the procedures to impeach Musharraf.

Whoever follows the visit sees that Raza Gilani submitted to America, and that America secured the People's Party's support for the candidate whom America puts forward for the presidency of the republic; and naturally Nawaz Sharif's party is guaranteed.

As a result of that visit, America gave the green light to the governing coalition for the procedures to impeach Musharraf, after it had secured the agreement of Raza Gilani, and consequently the People's Party, to support America's candidate for the presidency of the republic, such that the People's Party would not work to obstruct the arrival of whomever America wants to the presidency of the republic.

Raza Gilani, as an English agent, may have shown Bush agreement not to obstruct the arrival of whomever America wants to the presidency of the republic, in the manner the English follow in their policy of not confronting America; but the more likely is that America tempted him with a post of importance in the new authority, and that he has become close to America.

However, what is expected is that Britain will not keep silent about losing an opportunity that arose for it to participate in government in Pakistan since the mentioned deal. Therefore it will work, through leaders in the People's Party who are loyal to it, to obstruct the election of the next President of the Republic, unless it is guaranteed an effective participation in government along the lines of the previous deal.

Britain does not covet complete influence in Pakistan, but it will not let an opportunity that arose for it be lost. Therefore the obstruction of the election of the President of the Republic whom America wants, this obstruction is strongly possible, unless the talks on a new deal resume.

As for who the expected next President is, regardless of names, the effective role in nominating the President and electing him will be America's, and there are three possibilities:

The first possibility: that it is Raza Gilani himself, and that is if America is reassured that he has actually become loyal to it, and not in form only, in the new manner of the English of appearing to agree with America's policy and then stabbing it in secret. If America is reassured that Raza Gilani has actually become loyal to it, he has the best chance. But this matter requires calming Britain, which will not easily keep silent about this matter and may stir up problems for Raza Gilani from the leaders of the People's Party loyal to Britain.

The second possibility: from Nawaz Sharif's party, with priority to one of its leaders and not to Nawaz Sharif himself. Although he is one of America's men, he is relatively disliked among the people, besides the fact that the effects of the Kargil crisis have still not been erased from America's memory. America will not resort to nominating Nawaz Sharif unless it lacks another strong candidate from his party; then it may resort to him.

The third possibility: if the two previous possibilities prove impossible, America may resort to the army anew, especially since Kayani was appointed commander of the army on Musharraf's nomination and with America's agreement, and America will not lack a means to politicise the military according to America's eccentric democracy!

Finally we say: if only the agents would use their minds and take a lesson from what happens to their predecessors at the hands of the colonial states, which spit out their agent as a date stone is spat out when his role is exhausted, whereupon this spat-out agent loses his worldly life after he had already lost his Deen because of his agency to the Kuffar and his betrayal of his Ummah,

we say: if only the agents would understand this, they would at least preserve their worldly life by drawing close to their peoples and not to the colonialists, but they do not understand.

18 Sha'ban 1429 AH

19/8/2008 CE
